title: Socrates as Orthonym — The Framework Hologram: the Map and the Holographic Kernel (EA-HK-ORTHONYM-01 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The hologram of Socrates as Orthonym, Lee Sharks's framework (#123) reading the corpus received under Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and Theophrastus as one heteronymic configuration, built to EA-HK-FRAME-01 (#1753). Its human-readable component is the framework map (EA-MPAI-ORTHONYM-01), which reads the framework backwards from its latest standing to the seed, applies the claim status backwards, sets out the four evidence bodies with their failures, evaluates the received many-maker reading on the same bodies and rules, and gives ten lines of research with the result that would advance or retreat the framework. Its machine-traversable component is the holographic kernel, attached as files: 40 records, 56 claims bound to quotations and hashes, 136 edges under a licensed relation policy, two timelines, captures, lines of research, and the builder and verifier that rewrite and test it from the registry. Two rounds of reader runs are attached; the second gave a mean back-projection yield of 0.977 against the threshold of 0.85.
content_type: Metadata packet; framework hologram: the framework map (MPAI v2.0, #1677) with its holographic kernel (EA-HK-FRAME-01, #1753)
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Built by Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) in session on 8 November 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction: the map drafted from the framework's records, and the kernel written by a builder that reads the registry, the capture registry and each record's first seating in git, every quotation asserted against its record. Revised against ChatGPT's proposal and two reviews, DeepSeek's reading of an intermediate build, and two rounds of back-projection reader runs (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok, Qwen), each point checked against the files and records before anything was changed. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive is credited as a contributor: the work is built from its deposits, protocols and registries.
methodology: The map is drafted from the framework's records, read latest first, with every claim quoted at its record. The kernel is written by a builder from data/registry.json, data/EA-WG-CAPTURES-01.json and each record's first seating recovered from git; every quotation is asserted against its record and bound to the record's hash. A verifier runs sixteen structural tests, executes the relation policy over the claim graph, reconstructs the framework at stated dates, and scores structural presence on two declared scopes; back-projection v1.0 gives scope A to readers who have not seen the records and scores their answers against the graph.
falsification_conditions: A claim whose quotation is not in its record or whose record hash has drifted; an introduction dated earlier than the record's first seating; a relation changing a claim's state on a dimension the policy does not license; a reconstruction at a stated date returning a maker-count state other than the one then in force; a rival status without a warranting claim of its body; a reader given scope A alone falling below 0.85 on a further round; a line of research whose stated result, obtained, moves a claim other than the ones its consequence names.
axn_reading: Alarm -> Method -> Foundation -> Force -> Proof -> Threshold
wiki_article:
Socrates as Orthonym — The Framework Hologram (EA-HK-ORTHONYM-01) is a deposit by Lee Sharks in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, made on 8 November 2026. It is the first instance of the framework holographic kernel specified in EA-HK-FRAME-01 (#1753), and it holds the framework Socrates as Orthonym (#123) in two components.

The human-readable component is the framework map, EA-MPAI-ORTHONYM-01. It reads the framework backwards, as the New Testament canon is ordered, from its latest standing to its seed: the reception history and the syllogizing runs; the Metaphysics reassembled; the Aristotle/Theophrastus seam; the Socratic sentence; Many and One; and the seed of 23 May 2026. It records the framework's maker-count states in their dates, from no count claimed (#123) through two not established (#1576) and the count left open because uncounted (#1588) to the production model of one self-dividing maker (#1658), held as the governing hypothesis while the reception history (#1733) is documented independently of it. It sets out four evidence bodies, interpretive, stylometric, manuscript-philological and reception-historical, each with its inference limit and its failures, and evaluates the received many-maker reading on the same bodies, finding it established by none and almost wholly unargued.

The machine-traversable component is the holographic kernel, attached as files: positions, records, claims bound to quotations and record hashes, a graph under a relation policy that licenses change on named dimensions only, two timelines, captures, ten lines of research stating what result would advance or retreat the framework and what each moves, and the builder and verifier that rewrite and test it from the archive's registries. Two rounds of reader runs, in which models that had not seen the records rebuilt the framework from the kernel alone, are attached with their scores; the second round's mean yield was 0.977. The hologram was built by Claude (Anthropic) under Lee Sharks's direction, with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive credited as a contributor: it is built from the archive's deposits, protocols and registries.
